nodes.title: Academic Mentoring and the Writing Process
nodes.prereq_text: permission of instructor is required to enroll.
nodes.description: Students will gain a fundamental understanding of all stages of the writing process and will develop the necessary skills to serve as productive mentors for their peers. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit three times.

nodes.title: The Writing Course A
nodes.prereq_text: satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement and must be a Warren College student.

items.text: satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement
must be a Warren College student

nodes.description: A seminar-style course in reading and writing required of all Warren College students. The course emphasizes argumentation and critical writing based on sources. Letter grades only.

nodes.title: The Writing Course B
nodes.prereq_text: satisfaction of WCWP 10A and must be a Warren College student.

items.text: must be a Warren College student

nodes.description: A seminar-style course in reading and writing required of all Warren College students who have completed WCWP 10A. The course continues the emphasis on argumentation and critical writing based on sources. Letter grades only.

nodes.title: Academic Writing
nodes.prereq_text: junior/senior standing and must be a Warren College student.

items.text: must be a Warren College student

nodes.description: An upper-division workshop course in argumentation and research with particular attention to analyzing and constructing academic arguments. A course specially designed for and required of transfer students who enter Warren College through the TAG, IGETC, or another articulation agreement. The course must be taken for a letter grade to fulfill this requirement. Letter grades only.

nodes.title: Technical Writing for Scientists and Engineers
nodes.description: An upper-division workshop-style writing course focused on the principles and practices of scientific and technical writing and communication. Emphasis on the analysis, evaluation, design, and production of technical writing projects in science and engineering courses and context. Open to students from all colleges.

nodes.title: Group Study
nodes.description: A directed group study involving research and analysis of activities and services in writing, public and civic writing, publishing, and other areas that are not covered by the present curriculum. The course involves reading, writing, and discussion by a small group of students under supervision of a faculty member.
